successCriteria.description: Every one of the seven KnexLeaveRepository methods (findById, findAll, findByEmployeeId, findByStatus, create, update, delete) catches errors thrown by the Knex query builder / pg driver and never lets a raw Knex or pg error propagate to the caller.
When a Knex/pg error is caught, the repository throws a typed domain error (a distinct error type/class, not a raw Error or Knex error) so callers can identify repository failures by type.

The ILeaveRepository interface contract is unchanged — method names, parameter lists, and return types remain identical to the current declaration, and the existing leave.repository.test.ts suite still passes without modification.
A unit test exists that mocks the Knex instance to reject/throw on each repository method and asserts the repository surfaces the typed domain error (not the raw Knex/pg error) for every method.

Happy-path behavior of all seven methods is preserved — successful queries still return mapped LeaveRequest objects, null, arrays, or booleans exactly as before, verified by the existing passing tests.

constraints: GP-006 (no unhandled promise rejections): all async errors in repository methods must be caught and handled — no repository method may reject with an uncaught Knex/pg error.
HARNESS no-any rule (severity high): catch variables must be typed as `unknown` with type guards rather than `any`; no `any` introduced by the error-handling code.
GP-001 (repository pattern): database access stays inside the repository; the error translation must not move query logic out of KnexLeaveRepository or bypass the repository layer.
Strict TypeScript (strict null checks, no implicit any) must remain satisfied — the error-handling additions must compile cleanly under the existing tsconfig.
The ILeaveRepository interface and IBaseRepository<LeaveRequest> contract must not be altered — no new methods, no signature changes, no removed methods.
No new runtime dependencies may be added to package.json; error types must be implemented in-project (the project has no existing error-type library).
outOfScope: Error handling/wrapping in other repositories (employee, balance, policy, notification) — only KnexLeaveRepository is in scope for this phase.
Adding retry logic, circuit breakers, or connection-recovery behavior to the repository — this phase only translates errors, it does not retry or recover.
Changing the LeaveService, LeaveController, or route layers to consume the new error type — downstream consumers are a later phase.
Logging, metrics, or audit recording of repository errors (GP-004 concerns) — out of scope; the repository only translates and rethrows.
Altering the toLeaveRequest row mapper or the Knex query construction itself — only error wrapping is added; query behavior is unchanged.

ambiguities.description: No error types currently exist in the codebase (src/shared/error types.ts is referenced in ARCHITECTURE.md but is absent; no RepositoryError/DomainError class exists). The intent says "e.g., a RepositoryError or rethrow a typed domain error" but does not fix which. The implementer must decide whether to create a new RepositoryError class (and where it lives) versus reusing/creating a broader domain error hierarchy.
options: Introduce a single new RepositoryError class under src/shared (matching the ARCHITECTURE.md reference to shared error types)
Introduce a broader domain-error base class plus a RepositoryError subclass
Reuse an existing error type if one is discovered/added by a concurrent change

ambiguities.description: The intent allows either translating into a RepositoryError OR rethrowing a typed domain error. It is unclear whether all caught Knex/pg errors should map to one generic RepositoryError, or whether specific pg error codes (e.g., unique-violation, foreign-key violation, connection errors) should map to distinct typed errors.
options: Map every caught Knex/pg error to a single generic RepositoryError
Inspect pg error codes and map at least unique-violation / foreign-key / connection failures to distinct typed errors

ambiguities.description: It is unspecified whether the original Knex/pg error should be preserved as a `cause` on the translated error (for debugging) or discarded entirely. Preserving it aids diagnostics but could leak driver internals; GP-004 forbids logging sensitive data but does not directly govern error causes.
options: Preserve the original error as the `cause` of the translated error
Discard the original error and surface only the typed domain error

entityInvariants.invariant: The LeaveRequest domain entity shape and its mapping from raw database rows (via toLeaveRequest) must remain unchanged by the error-handling additions — successful reads still produce valid LeaveRequest objects with correct date parsing and null handling.

Every public method of KnexLeaveRepository is total with respect to database failures: it either returns its declared result type (on success) or throws a typed domain error (on Knex/pg failure) — it never rejects with a raw Knex or pg error.

The ILeaveRepository interface (extending IBaseRepository<LeaveRequest> with findByEmployeeId and findByStatus) must remain the unchanged public contract; KnexLeaveRepository must continue to implement it exactly.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: On Knex/pg failure, throws a typed domain error (not a raw Knex/pg error); on success returns LeaveRequest or null as before.
On Knex/pg failure, throws a typed domain error; on success returns LeaveRequest[] (possibly empty) as before.
On Knex/pg failure, throws a typed domain error; on success returns LeaveRequest[] as before.
On Knex/pg failure, throws a typed domain error; on success returns LeaveRequest[] as before.
On Knex/pg failure (e.g., constraint violation), throws a typed domain error; on success returns the created LeaveRequest as before.
On Knex/pg failure, throws a typed domain error; on success returns the updated LeaveRequest or null (when no row matched) as before.
On Knex/pg failure, throws a typed domain error; on success returns boolean (true if a row was deleted, false otherwise) as before.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The error-wrapping changes must preserve the existing KnexLeaveRepository method signatures, the TABLE_NAME constant, the constructor's optional-Knex-injection pattern (for testability), and the toLeaveRequest mapper behavior — only try/catch translation is added.
The IBaseRepository<T> interface (findById, findAll, create, update, delete) must remain unchanged; KnexLeaveRepository must still structurally satisfy it after error wrapping is added.

The existing repository test suite (happy-path coverage for all seven methods plus toLeaveRequest null/date handling) must continue to pass unmodified — the error wrapping must not alter observable success behavior.
No changes to the shared enums; the error type introduced must not duplicate or alter LeaveType/LeaveRequestStatus/LeaveBalanceStatus/EmployeeStatus.

The introduced error type should align with the ARCHITECTURE.md reference to shared error types (src/shared/error types.ts) — placing domain/repository error types under src/shared is consistent with the documented module layout.

integrationPoints.why: The repository's Knex instance is backed by the shared pg pool; error translation must handle errors originating from this connection layer without modifying it.
The typed domain error thrown by the repository is the contract future service-layer consumers will catch; the error type chosen now becomes the integration surface for the leave service.

integrationPoints.target: src/shared error types (referenced in ARCHITECTURE.md, not yet present)
integrationPoints.why: If a RepositoryError/domain error class is introduced, it should live in the shared error-types location the architecture documents, so other repositories can reuse the same translation pattern later.
